videos.script: A method that looks something up can find nothing. For most of Java's history it said so by returning null, and the caller found out three calls later, when something failed with a NullPointerException. {{npe}} Here is that failure, and the message Java prints for it now, which at least names the call that returned null. {{optional}} Optional is a box that is either empty or holds one value, and the return type says so before anybody runs the code. {{chain}} You do not open the box to use it. map, filter and orElse work on it as it is, and an empty box passes through all of them untouched. {{get}} And the one method that undoes the idea: get. Called on an empty box, it fails exactly like the null it replaced.
